Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. We're starting to onboard AMARCO as a multi-region reseller for Redwood’s hosting tier — most volume in the UK/EU and a chunk in India. Procurement asked us to share the vendor evidence needed so Redwood can create a single vendor record but split POs by entity when required.

Two quick clarifications:
- What specific VAT/GST evidence do you need from our UK and Indian legal entities to enable PO binding and automated invoice matching?
- Do you require separate vendor records per legal entity, or can you do a single vendor with multiple invoicing destinations?

Happy to provide the certificates. Attaching current VAT/GST PDFs now for visibility (we'll send the originals if needed).

Subject: Re: Vendor tax evidence and PO binding for resellers across UK / IN

Thanks Jonathan — good context. Outline below for what we need and next steps to get a PO bound. I'll loop in Tax/Procurement internally (Ben and Kim) for any edge cases.

What Redwood needs (quick checklist):
1) UK / EU sales (invoiced to AMARCO Ltd UK entity)
   - VAT registration certificate (matching legal name and registered address) — we can accept the PDF you attached.
   - Legal entity name as it should appear on the vendor record.
   - Preferred remittance email and billing contact.

2) India / APAC sales (if invoiced to an Indian legal entity)
   - GST registration / GSTIN certificate (PDF).
   - Clarify whether Indian entity will be the invoicing party or whether supplies are routed from the UK under a reseller agreement.

3) Invoicing format and PO matching
   - Redwood requires invoice line-level quantities or a PO reference that exactly matches the PO number we issue to the vendor. 
   - If a single vendor record is used for multiple legal entities, please tell us the mapping of which PO prefixes / legal-entity identifiers should route to which AP/AR entity in your org.

4) Intercompany / reverse-charge considerations
   - If AMARCO will invoice from the UK to Redwood EU entities and expects reverse charge or VAT-exempt treatment, we need a written confirmation of the tax reasoning and the VAT numbers for both parties.

Next steps to get PO bound on our side:
- Please complete the attached Redwood_VENDOR_SETUP_FORM.xlsx and return with the certificates (VAT/GST).
- We will open a vendor onboarding ticket and (depending on the entity mapping you provide) either create separate vendor records per legal entity or a parent record with invoicing destinations flagged.
- Once records are created, Procurement will issue a PO per legal entity as needed (you will receive the PO number(s) — please include them verbatim on invoices).

If you prefer, we can do a short 20-minute call to walk through the form — suggest Thu 12 Aug 10:00 BST.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Vendor tax evidence and PO binding for resellers across UK / IN

Naomi — quick internal note.

Thanks for the checklist. A couple of points for Tax (Irene) before we finalize whether to create two vendor records or a single parent:
- For Indian GST, we need to confirm whether AMARCO's Indian entity is supplying goods/services to Redwood India (local supply) or if the UK entity will invoice and Indian customers will be handled via resale. Treatment determines whether we should apply reverse charge on our side or accept local GST invoices and reclaim per Indian rules.
- If they plan to invoice from the UK for EU customers, we should request a written statement on where legal title/fulfillment occurs; we may need to include reverse-charge reasoning in vendor notes and on the PO.

Irene — can you confirm the minimum evidence we need to accept an Indian GST invoice for APAC spend (invoice language/fields, GSTIN format, IRN/ack number if available)? Also advise whether Redwood requires separate vendor IDs for tax-withholding purposes.

I'll hold off creating records until we get confirmation.

Ben
Procurement Lead — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
